title: The Pragmatic Programmer
author: David Thomas, Andrew Hunt
description: A guide to software craftsmanship, covering everything from personal responsibility and career development to architectural techniques for writing flexible, adaptable code.

title: Clean Code
author: Robert C. Martin
description: A handbook of agile software craftsmanship arguing that readable, well-named, small-function code is a professional obligation rather than a luxury.

title: Designing Data-Intensive Applications
author: Martin Kleppmann
description: The big ideas behind reliable, scalable and maintainable systems: replication, partitioning, transactions, consistency models and stream processing.

title: Refactoring
author: Martin Fowler
description: A catalogue of behaviour-preserving code transformations, plus the discipline of taking small safe steps backed by tests.

title: The Mythical Man-Month
author: Frederick P. Brooks Jr.
description: Essays on software engineering management, including the observation that adding people to a late project makes it later.

title: Domain-Driven Design
author: Eric Evans
description: How to tackle complexity in the heart of software by building a shared model and a ubiquitous language with domain experts.

title: Dune
author: Frank Herbert
description: On the desert planet Arrakis, control of the galaxy's most valuable substance turns a displaced noble heir into a prophesied leader.

title: Neuromancer
author: William Gibson
description: A burned-out console cowboy is hired for one last run through cyberspace by an employer whose motives are not remotely human.

title: The Left Hand of Darkness
author: Ursula K. Le Guin
description: An envoy to an ambisexual world on the brink of political catastrophe finds that his own assumptions are the hardest barrier to cross.

title: Project Hail Mary
author: Andy Weir
description: A lone astronaut wakes with no memory aboard a spacecraft, tasked with solving an extinction-level problem using nothing but first principles.

title: The Name of the Wind
author: Patrick Rothfuss
description: A legendary figure recounts his own history, from orphaned travelling performer to notorious student of arcane arts.

title: The Hobbit
author: J. R. R. Tolkien
description: A comfortable hobbit is swept into a company of dwarves on a long journey to reclaim a treasure guarded by a dragon.

title: A Wizard of Earthsea
author: Ursula K. Le Guin
description: A gifted young mage's pride summons something he cannot unmake, and the rest of his life becomes an attempt to face it.

title: Piranesi
author: Susanna Clarke
description: A man catalogues the tides and statues of an endless house, until evidence appears that his understanding of it is incomplete.

title: Nineteen Eighty-Four
author: George Orwell
description: A minor party functionary whose job is rewriting the past commits the crime of preferring the truth.

title: Beloved
author: Toni Morrison
description: A woman who escaped slavery is visited by a presence that will not let the past stay buried.

title: Never Let Me Go
author: Kazuo Ishiguro
description: Three friends from an unusual English boarding school gradually piece together the purpose their upbringing was designed to serve.

title: Klara and the Sun
author: Kazuo Ishiguro
description: An artificial friend observes the family that buys her with relentless attention and an entirely non-human theory of love.

title: The Big Sleep
author: Raymond Chandler
description: A private detective takes a blackmail case for a dying general and finds it attached to something considerably worse.

title: And Then There Were None
author: Agatha Christie
description: Ten strangers are lured to an island and accused, one by one, of a death nobody punished them for.

title: The Girl with the Dragon Tattoo
author: Stieg Larsson
description: A disgraced journalist and a brilliant, guarded investigator reopen a forty-year-old disappearance inside a powerful family.

title: Sapiens
author: Yuval Noah Harari
description: A single-volume account of how one species of ape came to dominate the planet through shared fictions and cooperative myth-making.

title: Guns, Germs, and Steel
author: Jared Diamond
description: An argument that geography and biogeography, rather than innate difference, shaped the unequal fates of human societies.

title: Thinking, Fast and Slow
author: Daniel Kahneman
description: Decades of research on the two systems that drive judgement: fast, intuitive, error-prone, and slow, effortful, easily tired.

title: Why We Sleep
author: Matthew Walker
description: What sleep does for memory, immunity and mood, and what happens across a population that treats it as optional.

title: The Selfish Gene
author: Richard Dawkins
description: Reframes evolution from the perspective of the replicator rather than the organism, and coins the idea of the meme along the way.

title: Surely You're Joking, Mr. Feynman!
author: Richard P. Feynman
description: Anecdotes from a physicist who treated safecracking, samba drumming and Nobel-winning physics as the same kind of curiosity.

title: The Innovators
author: Walter Isaacson
description: A group biography of the mathematicians, engineers and hackers whose collaborations produced the computer and the internet.

title: Meditations
author: Marcus Aurelius
description: Private notes written by a Roman emperor to himself on duty, mortality and the limits of what is within one's control.

title: The Lean Startup
author: Eric Ries
description: Treating a new venture as a series of experiments: build, measure, learn, and pivot before the runway ends.
